content: 1. Solifenacin affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor closely when using this drug. 2. Letermovir increases the levels of sorafenib by influencing the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Sotorasib decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the P-gp substrate for dosage modifications. Monitor closely. 4. Letermovir increases the levels of sparsentan by affecting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is needed. Regularly monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function when sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 5. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. Monitor closely. 6. Letermovir increases the levels of sufentanil by influencing the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of sufentanil with any CYP3A4 inhibitor may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, potentially leading to prolonged adverse effects, including fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely. 7. Letermovir increases the levels of sunitinib by affecting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Tacrolimus increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir increases the levels of tacrolimus by affecting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor tacrolimus plasma concentrations during treatment and after discontinuation of letermovir, and adjust the tacrolimus dose accordingly. Monitor closely. 9. Letermovir increases the levels of tadalafil by influencing the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Letermovir increases the levels of tamoxifen by affecting the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by influencing the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of tazemetostat with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the current dose of tazemetostat (refer to the drug monograph for dosage modifications). Monitor closely. 12. Telmisartan increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir increases the levels of telmisartan through other mechanisms (see comment). Use caution and monitor closely. Comment: Letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 13. Tenofovir AF decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 14. Tenofovir DF decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 15. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage if recommended in its approved product labeling. Monitor closely. 16. Teriflunomide increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 17. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of letermovir through other mechanisms (see comment). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Tipranavir decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 18. Trofinetide increases the levels or effects of letermovir through other mechanisms (see comment). Avoid or use an alternative drug. Trofinetide (an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor) may increase plasma levels of OATP1B1 or OATP1B3 substrates. Avoid co-administration with sensitive substrates. 19. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. Monitor closely. 20. Ublituximab decreases the effects of letermovir through immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Valsartan increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir increases the levels of valsartan through other mechanisms (see comment). Use caution and monitor closely. Comment: Letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of co-administered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 22. Vinblastine decreases the levels or effects of letermovir by acting on the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 23. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Either drug increases the toxicity of the other through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 24. Letermovir decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Closely monitor for reduced effectiveness of voriconazole. 25. Voxilaprevir increases the levels of letermovir by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 26. Letermovir increases the levels of zaleplon by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Letermovir increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg PO BID when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib. 28. Letermovir increases the levels of zileuton by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Letermovir increases the levels of ziprasidone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Letermovir increases the levels of zolpidem by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Common adverse effects of letermovir include nausea (27%), diarrhea (26%), vomiting (19%), peripheral edema (14%), cough (14%), headache (14%), fatigue (13%), abdominal pain (12%), tachycardia (4%), and atrial fibrillation (3%). 32. Letermovir is contraindicated with pimozide, ergot alkaloids, pitavastatin, or simvastatin when co-administered with cyclosporine due to significant drug interactions that may lead to adverse reactions or reduced therapeutic effects. 33. There is no data available regarding the use of letermovir in pregnant women. Animal studies have shown embryo-fetal developmental toxicity, including fetal malformations, in rats at exposures 11 times higher than human exposure at the recommended human dose (RHD). In rabbits, no embryo-fetal developmental toxicity was observed at exposures up to 2 times higher than human exposure at the RHD. 34. No data is available on the effect of letermovir on human fertility. Decreased fertility due to testicular toxicity was observed in male rats. 35. It is unknown if letermovir is present in human breast milk, affects human milk production, or has effects on the breastfed child. In lactating rats, letermovir was present in the milk and the blood of nursing pups. The benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and potential adverse effects on the child. 36. Letermovir solution must be diluted before IV administration. Inspect the vial for discoloration and particulate matter before dilution. The solution should appear clear and colorless. Do not use if discolored or if visible particles are present. Do not shake the vial. 37. Use compatible IV bags and infusion set materials. Letermovir is not recommended for use with polyurethane-containing IV administration set tubing. Once diluted, the solution ranges from colorless to yellow, and variations in color do not affect product quality. Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before administration. 38. IV administration should not exceed 4 weeks. Administer the entire contents of the IV bag via infusion over 1 hour using a peripheral catheter or central venous line. Do not administer as an IV bolus. 39. Letermovir injection, containing hydroxypropyl betadex, should only be used in patients unable to take oral therapy. Switch to oral administration as soon as possible.
